top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Jedermann-Rennen Rund um Köln's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
51ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
75 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.

Road-specific control matters at Jedermann-Rennen Rund um Köln. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 75 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Jedermann-Rennen Rund um Köln. Train it until it feels boring.
At Jedermann-Rennen Rund um Köln, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,839ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Jedermann-Rennen Rund um Köln. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
